sentences.text: The fossil record of Parringtonia is fragmentary, preserving only a right maxilla, a left scapula, a partial ischium, nine vertebrae, and five osteoderms.
Its maxilla held five tooth sockets and featured a foramen on the outer surface, a trait not seen in the related genus Erpetosuchus.
The shoulder blade is distinguished by a small tubercle located directly over the shoulder socket.
Evidence of unfused vertebrae indicates that this individual died while still immature.
Erpetosuchids possess an exceptionally large tuber on the scapula compared to other archosauriforms.
Parringtonia is known from a single fossil specimen discovered in the Anisian-age Manda Formation of Tanzania.
Parringtonia shares similarities with Erpetosuchus, a related archosaur found in Scotland and the eastern United States.
Parringtonia is an extinct Triassic archosaur genus within the family Erpetosuchidae, represented by the type species Parringtonia gracilis.
It was placed in the family Erpetosuchidae in 1970 and 1976 due to similarities in its scapula with Erpetosuchus, and Nesbitt and Butler redescribed it in 2012.

The family is defined by teeth restricted to the front of the maxilla, a posterior maxilla thicker than tall, and a lack of tooth serrations. Recent analyses place Erpetosuchidae within the clade Suchia as the sister group to Aetosauria and Revueltosaurus.
Parringtonia lived during the Anisian age of the Triassic period.
The phylogenetic placement of Parringtonia is debated, with some studies suggesting a relationship to Crocodylomorpha, though this is now questioned.
